content.text:
Fixed. `.default(fn)` and `.prefault(fn)` inside `z.object()` were running their function twice per parse. Now they run once.

**Cause:** the cycle check in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/memoizer.ts` (`isRecursive`) walks every key of a schema's `def` looking for child schemas. `defaultValue` is a getter that calls the user's function, so the walk ran the default once and the real parse ran it again. A bare `z.string().default(fn)` was unaffected because the check only runs when an object is parsed.

**Fix:** the walk now skips the `defaultValue` key. It only ever holds the default value, never a child schema. I couldn't just skip every getter: `catchall` on merged object defs is also a getter and can hold a schema that matters for spotting cycles.

**Test:** I added one to `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/default.test.ts`. It checks that a default and a prefault inside an object each run exactly once and give the right output.

**Results:** the `zod` test project passed 5164 of 5166 tests. The two failures are in `treeshake.test.ts`, and I don't think they come from this change. esbuild can't find the entry file because the Windows path loses its backslashes (`C:UsersUSER...`), and that code doesn't touch the memoizer. I didn't re-run that file without my change to confirm.

**Compile mode isn't verified.** In this setup, the `compile-mode` project loads zod's core from a different checkout (`b15/base/z6495`) through the shared `node_modules`, so it doesn't see this edit and the new test will fail there. Its stack trace showed the same extra call from the same check, so the fix should cover it once that project loads this folder's code, but I haven't seen it pass.

I didn't measure speed, memory or bundle size: it's a one-line change on a path that runs once per schema, and its result is cached.
